## Purpose

Explain why a COMPLETED child of a collecting parent was never assembled into
the parent's branch, and advance it for exactly the head a dry run reported. A
collecting parent assembles a child only once approved review evidence pins
the child's exact checkpoint head, and `delivery_promote` re-checks that
evidence before it pushes. Until a child is assembled no receipt reaches the
parent, and every sibling whose `needs` names it stays out of the claim
frontier.

## When a playbook uses it

It is a supervisor/operator control (`aq integration redrive-child TASK_ID`),
not a playbook step. The collector records completion evidence for a child
whose published head proves out on its own; the supervisor runs this when
`aq doctor --check integration.stuck_children` still lists a child.

## How it works internally

`_cmd_integration_redrive_child` (`src/commands/integration_commands.py`)
authorizes the caller with `integration_operator` and calls
`ChildDelivery.run` (`src/integration/child_delivery.py`). The diagnosis reads
the child, its checkpoint, its branch origin, its parent's checkpoint and live
collection operation, its receipts, promotion intents and review verdicts,
then proves the head in the retained repository the promotion service
fetches: the remote branch tip is the recorded head, the head descends from
the child's origin base, and its tree resolves. Applying re-runs the
diagnosis, refuses a head that differs from `expected_head_sha` (`changed`),
re-reads the child under the project's hierarchy lock, appends approved `leaf`
evidence for that head and tree, and asks the parent's collector to queue the
child's `delivery.ready` now (`CollectionService.collect_parent`).

## Side effects and persistence

A dry run writes nothing. Applying appends one `integration_review_evidence`
row (`reviewer_identity` is the operator, `evidence.decision_path` is
`operator_redrive`, `evidence.reason` the audit reason), may enqueue one
`delivery.ready` outbox event, and logs one `integration.child_redriven`
event. Re-applying reuses the existing approved row. Promotion, the receipt
and the parent's readiness follow through the normal collection path.

## Failure modes and diagnostics

- `not_found` / `not_eligible`: unknown task, not a hierarchy/train project, a
  root (use `aq integration redrive-root`), not COMPLETED, a nested parent, or
  no integration checkpoint.
- `nothing_to_redrive`: already delivered into the parent, or a promotion of
  this head is already being written or repaired.
- `blocked`: a reviewer rejected the head or is still open, the remote branch
  moved or is unpublished, the head does not descend from the origin base, the
  checkpoint is still the origin base (a no-code child takes `aq integration
  record-noop`), or the parent is not collecting. `reason` names which; report
  it, do not force it.
- `changed`: the head moved since the dry run, or the child changed before the
  evidence commit. Run the dry run again.

## Example step

```bash
aq integration redrive-child sharp-impact.1
aq integration redrive-child sharp-impact.1 --apply \
  --head ef91fb3550c0bd61d885b51022ef666371b0e67a --reason "child closed, never assembled"
```
